newsitem.title: UK: UK plans to plug telecoms tax loophole.
newsitem.headline: UK plans to plug telecoms tax loophole.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it planned to close a loophole which allows suppliers based outside the European Union to sell telecoms services in the UK without charging value added tax (VAT).

Under proposals outlined in Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's 1996 budget -- which will need agreement from all member states -- telecom services will be liable to VAT when supplied to UK customers by non-EU suppliers.
Suppliers based in the UK will also no longer have to charge VAT on sales outside the EU -- or to business customers in other member states of the European Community.
Clarke said 800 million stg per year of existing revenue would be protected under the proposed plans, the precise terms and implementation date of which have yet to be finalised and agreed.

The plans, which would affect cable and satellite broadcasting services, Internet access supplies and electronic message delivery services such as E-mail, would also stop distorting competition by ensuring non-European Union companies no longer had any VAT advantage over UK-based suppliers.
Under current rules, telekom services are liable to VAT in the country where the supplier is established.
UK and other EU suppliers charge VAT to all their customers inside and outside the EU whereas companies based outside can supply identical services VAT-free.

The government's Customs and Excise department said in a statement that this had led to revenue losses because exempt businesses and others, who could not fully recover VAT on their purchases, had exploited the rules to avoid tax.

"The revenue yield from this measure is estimated at around 10 million stg per year, and rising," it said. "If unchecked, the revenue loss could rise ultimately to the order of 800 million stg per year."
The government plans to introduce provisions in its Finance Bill to prevent any revised rules being circumvented by advance payments and to provide what it called "transitional arrangements".
